Comprehensive Software Engineering Project Report

Covering SDLC, System Architecture, ERD, DFDs, Data Dictionary & UI Screenshots

Project Title: MBC Online Food Ordering System

Prepared For: Academic & Technical Project Submission
Date: September 2026

Executive Summary

The Malek Bateta Center (MBC) Online Food Ordering and Restaurant Management System is a web application designed to digitize ordering, inventory, and customer management for a famous traditional eatery based in Dhoraji, Gujarat (established in 1983).

The primary objective of this project is to provide customers with an intuitive online menu ordering platform featuring real-time cart handling, takeaway/delivery order options, and flexible payment methods (Cash on Delivery, UPI). Simultaneously, it equips restaurant administrators with a comprehensive management portal to monitor live customer orders, manage food item categories, update order fulfillment status, update site settings, and print formatted tax invoices.

Chapter 1: System Overview & Project Scope

1.1 Background & Problem Statement

Traditional food outlets face significant operational challenges when relying on manual pen-and-paper order taking, telephone calls, and physical queues. Key bottlenecks include order entry errors, communication delays during peak hours, inability to track live order delivery status, and fragmented sales records.

1.2 Objectives

  • Provide an accessible, responsive web application for customers to browse food items, customize orders, and place online food orders seamlessly.
  • Centralize order processing into a unified real-time admin portal with instant status updates (Pending → Preparing → Out for Delivery → Completed).
  • Automate tax and delivery fee calculations with dynamic invoice print generation.
  • Maintain an audit trail of user registrations, reviews, contact messages, and item catalogs in a normalized relational database.

Chapter 2: Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)

The MBC Food Ordering System was built following an Agile-Waterfall Hybrid SDLC Model. This approach combined structured phase-by-phase design deliverables with iterative sprint execution.

  • Phase 1: Requirement Analysis & Feasibility Study — Stakeholder interviews with restaurant staff and customers to capture core operational requirements.
  • Phase 2: System & Architectural Design — High-level system architectural models, process flow specifications, and DFDs.
  • Phase 3: Database Design & Data Modeling — Normalized database tables (3NF) in MySQL with PK/FK constraints.
  • Phase 4: System Implementation & Coding — Backend logic in PHP with PDO/MySQLi and Bootstrap 5 frontend UI.
  • Phase 5: Verification & System Testing — Component unit testing, integration testing, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
  • Phase 6: Deployment & Maintenance — Apache web server & MySQL deployment with routine backup protocols.

Chapter 7: Conclusion & Future Scope

The MBC Food Ordering and Restaurant Management System successfully digitizes traditional restaurant workflows into a modern, responsive web application. The platform streamlines online food ordering for customers and provides administrators with an efficient order fulfillment dashboard.
